jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Zimbabwe's only binding AI-relevant rules are the automated-decision provisions of the Cyber and Data Protection Act and its 2024 licensing regulations, which bar solely automated decisions with legal effects and automated decisions on children's data, enforced by the telecoms regulator POTRAZ as Data Protection Authority. POTRAZ also published a 2023 assessment of AI in the postal and telecommunications sector. The ICT ministry's National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2026-2030, launched in March 2026, plans a National AI Council, an AI ethics board, a future AI law and a regulatory sandbox; Cabinet has approved a National AI Charter to implement it, but the Charter text is not yet published.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Information Communication Technology, Postal and Courier Services
Postal and Telecommunications Regulatory Authority of Zimbabwe (POTRAZ)
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 12 October 2026 from documents read in full on the ICT ministry's and POTRAZ's websites. The National AI Strategy 2026-2030 was added in November 2026 once the ministry's own pages stated its March 2026 launch; the National AI Charter and the Child Online Protection Policy 2026-2030 are tracked as leads until their texts or dates are published officially. Not yet verified from the official text: pending bills before Parliament and any central bank AI guidelines.

instruments.english_title: Cyber and Data Protection Act [Chapter 12:07] (Act No. 5 of 2021)
instruments.current_status: In force since 3 December 2021 (date of commencement stated in the consolidated text). Enacted as Act No. 5 of 2021 (originally headed Data Protection Act); re-gazetted with its new title on 11 March 2022 per the Law Reviser's note. POTRAZ also publishes the 2021 Act as gazetted (Data-Protection-Act-5-of-2021.pdf) and the Ministry of ICT links a copy. Implemented by S.I. 155 of 2024; POTRAZ opened a consultation in October 2026 on administrative penalties (see leads).
instruments.summary: Zimbabwe's data protection and cybersecurity law, which designates POTRAZ as the Data Protection Authority, establishes a Cyber Security Centre and sets rules for processing personal data wholly or partly by automated means. Section 25 gives data subjects the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, that produces legal or similarly significant effects, unless they consented or the decision is based on law; section 20 requires controllers to notify the Authority before automated processing operations. It also amends the Criminal Law Code on cyber-crime and electronic evidence.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Only binding Zimbabwean law with explicit rules on automated decision-making and profiling; governs data used to train and run AI systems.

instruments.current_status: In force. S.I. 155 of 2024, published in the Supplement to the Zimbabwean Government Gazette dated 13 September 2024. In October 2026 POTRAZ published a consultation paper and draft amendment regulations introducing administrative penalties (see leads).
instruments.summary: Statutory Instrument 155 of 2024, made by the ICT Minister under section 32 of the Cyber and Data Protection Act, introduces licensing of data controllers, data protection officer appointments, security and breach-notification rules. Section 10(3) bars data controllers from subjecting a data subject to a decision based solely on automated processing with legal effects without consent or a legal basis, and section 10(5)(f) prohibits automated decision-making on children's data that affects children's rights; contraventions are offences punishable by a fine up to level 11 or up to seven years' imprisonment.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding regulation that turns the Act's automated-decision right into a controller obligation backed by criminal penalties and adds a specific ban on automated decisions about children.

instruments.summary: POTRAZ survey-based assessment of AI adoption by licensed telecommunications operators and postal and courier operators, covering adoption levels, use cases, AI strategies, barriers, skills, investment and regulatory support. It finds low adoption and recommends a multi-stakeholder AI and/or Big Data steering committee, better access to data for AI, a light-touch regulatory framework for responsible AI and a national focus on AI research, innovation and skills.

instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Information Communication Technology, Postal and Courier Services
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Information Communication Technology, Postal and Courier Services
instruments.current_status: Zimbabwe's first national AI strategy, covering 2026-2030. The Ministry of ICT, Postal and Courier Services states on its own news pages that the President launched the strategy in March 2026; the document itself prints no date. The ministry publishes the strategy in its official documents section (the copy carries a 'Distributed by Veritas' line). The strategy plans a National AI Council, an AI Strategy Implementation Office, an AI Ethics Board, a National AI Act and an AI regulatory sandbox; none of these had been set up by an instrument found so far. Cabinet has since approved a National AI Charter for implementing the strategy (text not yet published).
instruments.summary: Zimbabwe's first national AI strategy, issued by the Ministry of ICT, Postal and Courier Services with a foreword by the President, sets six pillars: AI talent and capacity, infrastructure and computational sovereignty, adoption and service transformation, AI governance, ethics and regulation, research and innovation, and international collaboration. For governance it proposes a multi-sectoral National AI Council, an AI Strategy Implementation Office, a National Data Agency and an AI Ethics Board, and commits to AI-specific legislation (a National AI Act), a revised data protection law and regulatory sandboxes. It includes flagship initiatives, a phased implementation roadmap and a monitoring and evaluation framework.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: The national AI policy framework; sets Zimbabwe's planned AI institutions, ethics oversight and legislative agenda.
metadata_gaps: Exact day of publication not stated on an official government page; month taken from the ministry's statement that the President launched the strategy in March 2026

leads.title: Zimbabwe National AI Charter
leads.issuing_authority: Ministry of Information Communication Technology, Postal and Courier Services
leads.note: News reports (ZBC, undated, about three months after the 13 March 2026 strategy launch, https://www.zbcnews.co.zw/?p=61520; Herald on the AI4I programme of 27 July-1 August 2026) describe the Charter as finalised. The ICT Minister described it as a values-based framework for ethical, transparent, inclusive and accountable AI underpinning the National AI Strategy and announced its launch. No official text found. If published, likely categories ethics and government governance. The same reports say terms of reference for a National Digital Regulatory Committee are finalised (not AI-specific). Status check 22 Nov 2026: the Ministry of ICT's news item 'Cabinet Approves National AI Charter' (https://ictministry.gov.zw/pages/article.html?id=2) states that Cabinet has approved the Zimbabwe National AI Charter, presented by the Minister of Finance as chair of the Cabinet Committee on National Development; it describes a governance framework with strategic oversight, institutional coordination and complaints-handling mechanisms. The page gives no Cabinet meeting date and the Charter text is not published, so it stays a lead.

leads.title: Zimbabwe National Child Online Protection Policy 2026-2030

leads.note: Official document on ictministry.gov.zw (documents section, https://ictministry.gov.zw/api/documents/8/download); no stated publication date. Read 22 Nov 2026 (44 pages): it contains AI commitments, including that Government shall expressly criminalise AI-generated child sexual abuse material (including deepfakes), introduce a mandatory AI Child Safety Impact Assessment for digital service providers deploying AI systems accessible to children, and require child-specific safeguards for AI-driven recommendation or ranking systems. Record (public-sector/risk-assurance/generative-ai) once an official launch or approval date is found.
